name.text: Spearman's Rank Correlation and Coefficient of Determination Analysis

questiontext.text:
Find the Spearman's ranks correlation coefficient between the two sets of variables given below and interpret the results

X \({@x1@}\) \({@x2@}\) \({@x3@}\) \({@x4@}\) \({@x5@}\) \({@x6@}\) \({@x7@}\) \({@x8@}\)
Y \({@y1@}\) \({@y2@}\) \({@y3@}\) \({@y4@}\) \({@y5@}\) \({@y6@}\) \({@y7@}\) \({@y8@}\)

Sperman rank correlation coefficient \(r=\) [[input:ans1]]. [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

From the sperman rank correlation coefficient we can say that [[input:ans3]].[[validation:ans3]][[feedback:prt3]]

Note: Give your answer correct to \(3 \) decimal places.

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

X Y Rank X Rank Y d \(=\) Rank X\(-\)Rank Y \(\text{d}^2\)
\({@x1@}\) \({@y1@}\) \({@rank_x[1]@}\) \({@rank_y[1]@}\) \({@rank_x[1]-rank_y[1]@}\) \({@(rank_x[1]-rank_y[1])^2@}\)
\({@x2@}\) \({@y2@}\) \({@rank_x[2]@}\) \({@rank_y[2]@}\) \({@rank_x[2]-rank_y[2]@}\) \({@(rank_x[2]-rank_y[2])^2@}\)
\({@x3@}\) \({@y3@}\) \({@rank_x[3]@}\) \({@rank_y[3]@}\) \({@rank_x[3]-rank_y[3]@}\) \({@(rank_x[3]-rank_y[3])^2@}\)
\({@x4@}\) \({@y4@}\) \({@rank_x[4]@}\) \({@rank_y[4]@}\) \({@rank_x[4]-rank_y[4]@}\) \({@(rank_x[4]-rank_y[4])^2@}\)
\({@x5@}\) \({@y5@}\) \({@rank_x[5]@}\) \({@rank_y[5]@}\) \({@rank_x[5]-rank_y[5]@}\) \({@(rank_x[5]-rank_y[5])^2@}\)
\({@x6@}\) \({@y6@}\) \({@rank_x[6]@}\) \({@rank_y[6]@}\) \({@rank_x[6]-rank_y[6]@}\) \({@(rank_x[6]-rank_y[6])^2@}\)
\({@x7@}\) \({@y7@}\) \({@rank_x[7]@}\) \({@rank_y[7]@}\) \({@rank_x[7]-rank_y[7]@}\) \({@(rank_x[7]-rank_y[7])^2@}\)
\({@x8@}\) \({@y8@}\) \({@rank_x[8]@}\) \({@rank_y[8]@}\) \({@rank_x[8]-rank_y[8]@}\) \({@(rank_x[8]-rank_y[8])^2@}\)

\(\displaystyle \sum d^{2}={@total_d_squared@}\)

\(n=\) no. of ranks \(=8\)

Spearman rank correlation coefficient \(\displaystyle r=1- \frac{ 6\sum d^2}{n(n^2-1)}\)

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle r &=1- \frac{6({@total_d_squared@})}{8(64-1)}\\ &=1-\frac{{@6*total_d_squared@}}{504}=1-{@(6*total_d_squared)/504@}\\ &={@ta1@}\\ \end{align} \)

Correct to three decimal places, the value of the coefficient is \({@ta1@}\). So we can say that {@mcq_correct(ta3)[1]@} .
